newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Optus Vision says subscribers over 100,000.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Optus Vision says subscribers over 100,000.

text.p: Australian unlisted pay television operator, Optus Vision, said on Thursday it had in excess of 100,000 pay television subscribers, which it said was a little higher than others had expected.
"At this moment, Optus Vision has in excess of 100,000 pay television subscribers," Optus vision managing director Geoff Cousins told reporters.
Cousins said that Optus Vision had installed cables passed over a million homes in its first year of operations, but that not all of these cables were active.
Penetration rates -- the number of pay television subscribers to the number of homes passed -- were higher than they appeared.

He also said that Optus Vision penetration rates were higher than those of its other pay television competitors, Australis Media Ltd and Foxtel, which is owned jointly by state-owned telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp and News Corp Ltd.
"If you look at the figures we've released, the penetration of Optus Vision is substantially ahead of its competitors," Cousins said.
He said Optus Vision would be adding five new pay television channels by the end of January 1997 -- the Warner movie Channel, one Arabic Channel, one Italian Channel and two Greek Channels.

Cousins said after a year of operations it was clear that Optus Vision had won the main strategic battles with its main cable competitor Foxtel. "As far as the major strategic battles are concerned they're over and Optus Vision is absolutely in the winning position," he said.
He said Optus Visions alliances with the Warner Group, the Disney Organisation and Channels seven and nine in Australia showed it had won the strategic battle for programming.
Cousins said Optus Vision was satisfied with its current churn rates.
Pay television operators refer to the loss of subscribers and the signing on of new subscribers as "churning".
"For us we're very satisfied with the churn rates and they're coming down and we'd expect them to come down much further once we've got many more telephony customers on board," he said.
"When you have those good services you get higher penetration and lower churning."
Optus Vision is 46.5 percent owned by both Australian telecommunications carrier Optus Communications and Continental CableVision Inc, which has merged with U.S. West.
The balance of Optus Vision is owned by Seven Network Ltd and Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd.
Optus Communications, which plans to float late in 1996, is 24.5 percent owned each by BellSouth Corp and Cable and Wireless Plc.
Cousins said Optus Vision aimed to offer its customers on-line services for internet use within the next six months, on top of the already available local telephone and pay television services.
"We do expect to have on-line services up and running in the first quarter of next year," he said.

He also said Optus Vision's pay television services would be available throughout Australia, either by optic fibre or by satellite from July 1997. He added this would happen regardless of whether or not a planned joint venture with Australis went ahead. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
